title: Pujith, Hemasiri get death sentence over Easter attacks | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 1 August 2026 01:31
-     - 9

Former IGP Pujith Jayasundara

Former Defence Secretary Hemasiri Fernando

Trial-at-Bar convicts former Police Chief and former Defence Secretary after Supreme Court-ordered retrial

 Majority bench finds both guilty of failing to act on prior intelligence warnings

A three-judge Colombo Trial-at-Bar yesterday sentenced former Inspector General of Police (IGP) Pujith Jayasundara and former Defence Secretary Hemasiri Fernando to death after finding them guilty on multiple charges, including criminal dereliction of duty for failing to act on intelligence warnings that preceded the 2019 Easter Sunday terrorist attacks.

The judgments followed retrials ordered by the Supreme Court after it set aside the pair’s earlier acquittals, holding that the Trial-at-Bar had erred in law by acquitting the accused without first calling upon them to present their defence.

The Attorney General had separately indicted Jayasundara and Fernando on charges including criminal negligence, criminal dereliction of duty and related offences arising from their alleged failure to act on intelligence information warning of the imminent Easter Sunday attacks.

On 18 February 2022, the then Trial-at-Bar acquitted both accused at the close of the prosecution’s case without calling for their defence.

The Attorney General subsequently appealed to the Supreme Court, arguing that the acquittals were contrary to law.

Allowing the appeal, the Supreme Court ruled that the accused should have been called upon to present their defence before any verdict was delivered. It set aside the acquittals and directed that the cases be retried.

Following the retrials, the Colombo Trial-at-Bar convicted both Jayasundara and Fernando, finding they had failed to take action to prevent the Easter Sunday attacks despite receiving prior intelligence warnings.

The judgments were delivered by the Trial-at-Bar comprising Judges Priyantha Liyanage, Viraj Weerasuriya and Tilakaratne Bandara.

Jayasundara was convicted and sentenced to death by a majority decision, with Judges Priyantha Liyanage and Tilakaratne Bandara finding him guilty, while Judge Viraj Weerasuriya dissented and acquitted the former IGP.

Fernando was also sentenced to death after being found guilty by the Trial-at-Bar on charges including criminal dereliction of duty for failing to act on prior intelligence warnings relating to the Easter Sunday attacks.

title: Govt. lines up policy changes to support $ 5 b digital exports | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 1 August 2026 01:25
-     - 10

Digital Economy Deputy Minister Eng. Eranga Weeraratne

Chief Adviser to the President on Digital Economy Dr. Hans Wijayasuriya

Cabinet paper on ‘Fund of Funds’ due within weeks to expand venture capital financing

 Capital mobility, venture capital tax changes and virtual SEZ among planned reforms

 Procurement overhaul to widen Government contracts for local technology firms

 AI, research and IP initiatives to support digital industry growth

The Government is preparing tax, regulatory and procurement reforms, including changes to venture capital taxation, capital mobility and public procurement, as it seeks to support a target of generating $ 5 billion in digital exports by 2030.

Speaking at the national validation workshop on Sri Lanka’s proposed digital export roadmap yesterday, Digital Economy Deputy Minister Eng. Eranga Weeraratne and GovTech Sri Lanka Chairman and Chief Adviser to the President on Digital Economy Dr. Hans Wijayasuriya outlined a series of policy measures aimed at improving access to finance, reducing regulatory barriers and encouraging technology companies to establish and expand their operations from Sri Lanka. 

The Deputy Minister said the Government expects to submit a Cabinet paper within weeks to establish a Fund of Funds under a national fund-of-funds policy to strengthen venture capital financing for startups.

Dr. Wijayasuriya said the Government is also finalising reforms to address tax pass-through issues affecting venture capital funds, while capital mobility rules will be revised to allow startups receiving foreign investment to use those funds for overseas expansion.

He said the measures are intended to address one of the industry’s long-standing challenges by making Sri Lanka a more attractive location for technology companies to retain their headquarters.

“We are looking at some of the root causes and creating an environment which encourages headquartering in Sri Lanka,” Dr. Wijayasuriya said. 

The Government is also developing a virtual Special Economic Zone that would allow technology companies to incorporate and operate virtually with fewer administrative barriers. Dr. Wijayasuriya said the initiative draws on models adopted in the UAE and several Eastern European countries to attract investment from smaller, high-growth technology firms.

Another priority is procurement reform aimed at enabling Government institutions to purchase technology solutions from smaller domestic companies through more agile procurement processes.

Dr. Wijayasuriya said the Government should become a platform for the private sector by creating opportunities for local firms to develop digital solutions for public institutions while supporting the growth of the domestic technology industry. 

The Government also plans to introduce incentive programs for research and intellectual property, alongside an Applied AI Institution and an AI Centre of Excellence as part of its digital economy agenda, Deputy Minister Weeraratne said. 

He said Government could establish the policy framework, but achieving the export target would depend on commitments from industry, investors and academia.

“Government alone cannot bring the full roadmap to fruition. We can bring out the right policies. But it is the industry who can actually make this happen,” he said. 

The proposals were presented during the validation workshop yesterday organised by the Digital Economy Ministry, GovTech Sri Lanka and the World Bank Group, where industry representatives, investors, academia and policymakers reviewed the draft roadmap before it is finalised.

title: Pujith, Hemasiri taken  to prison after sentencing | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 1 August 2026 01:22
-     - 11

Former Inspector General of Police (IGP) Pujith Jayasundara and former Defence Secretary Hemasiri Fernando were taken into prison custody yesterday after the Colombo Permanent High Court Trial-at-Bar sentenced them to death over their failure to prevent the 2019 Easter Sunday terrorist attacks despite receiving prior intelligence warnings.

The majority decision of the three-judge bench found both former officials guilty of charges including criminal dereliction of duty and aiding and abetting murder, ruling that they failed to take necessary action despite intelligence indicating an imminent series of coordinated suicide bombings.

The case relates to the 21 April 2019 Easter Sunday attacks targeting churches and hotels across Sri Lanka, which killed 260 people and injured hundreds, including foreign nationals.

Prosecutors had argued that Jayasundara and Fernando failed to carry out their official responsibilities by not implementing preventive security measures after receiving intelligence warnings on the planned attacks.

title: Colombo Port records 11.9% growth in 1H container throughput | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 1 August 2026 01:20
-     - 5

Ports and Civil Aviation Minister Anura Karunathilaka (left) and SLPA Chairman Dr. Parakrama Dissanayake, at an inspection visit at the new SLPA central building construction site

The Colombo Port has handled 4,444,034 Twenty-foot Equivalent Units (TEUs) during the first six months of 2026, representing an 11.9% increase compared to 3,972,053 TEUs handled during the corresponding period in 2025.

Transshipment continued to be the Port’s main business, accounting for 84.7% of total container throughput. Transshipment volumes increased by 12.6% over the corresponding period of the previous year, while domestic container volumes recorded a healthy growth of 8.3%.

Among the Port’s container terminals, Colombo International Container Terminals (CICT) handled 1,642,647 TEUs, accounting for 37% of the Colombo Port’s total container throughput during the six-month period.

The Port also recorded positive growth in vessel arrivals. During the first half of 2026, a total of 2,066 vessels called at the Port, compared to 2,016 vessels during the corresponding period in 2025, representing an overall increase of 2.5%.

Container vessel arrivals increased from 1,782 in 2025 to 1,797 in 2026, reflecting a 0.8% growth. Break-bulk vessel arrivals recorded a remarkable 55.6% increase, while liquid bulk vessel arrivals rose by 5.3%. Vessel calls for value-added maritime services—including bunkering, ship repairs, and chandelling—increased from 86 to 107, representing a significant 24.4% growth.

The Colombo Port continues to strengthen its position as one of the world’s leading container ports and is steadily progressing towards becoming one of the top 15 busiest container ports globally. This progress is being driven by several strategic initiatives, including expanding terminal capacity through new developments, investing in state-of-the-art ship-to-shore cranes and yard equipment, accelerating the digitalisation of port operations, reducing vessel turnaround and waiting times, strengthening customs coordination, enhancing international marketing efforts, and expanding logistics and maritime services beyond traditional cargo handling.

Sri Lanka Ports Authority Chairman Dr. Parakrama Dissanayake said that the sustained growth reflects the confidence that global shipping lines and customers continue to place in the Port of Colombo. 

“As we expand capacity and modernise our operations, our focus remains on delivering world-class port services with greater efficiency, reliability, and sustainability. Growth must be sustainable. We aim not only to increase throughput but also to enhance productivity, connectivity, profitability, and customer satisfaction,” he added.

title: Dockyard marks 52 years with return to quarterly profitability | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 1 August 2026 01:16
-     - 8

Stronger ship repair performance, improved cost efficiencies and lower finance expenses drive first positive quarter following an extended loss-making period

Managing Director/CEO 

Thimira S. Godakumbura

Colombo Dockyard PLC yesterday said it has recorded a financial turnaround for the three months ended 30 June 2026, returning to quarterly profitability following an extended period of losses.

The achievement comes as Colombo Dockyard prepares to mark its 52nd anniversary today, providing a significant milestone in the company’s ongoing transformation and renewed strategic direction following its collaboration with parent company Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Ltd.

The group recorded a Profit After Tax of Rs. 80.2 million for the quarter, reversing the Rs. 813.4 million loss reported during the corresponding period of 2025. Profit attributable to the owners of the company amounted to Rs. 86.3 million, while earnings per share improved to 22 cents from a restated loss per share of Rs. 3.51 during the corresponding period of the previous year.

Despite Group revenue declining by 6.8% to Rs. 5.84 billion during the quarter, improved cost efficiencies supported a substantial increase in profitability. 

Cost of sales declined by 21.8% to Rs. 4.63 billion, enabling gross profit to increase by 250.7% to Rs. 1.21 billion. The Group’s gross profit margin consequently improved to approximately 20.7%, compared with 5.5% during the corresponding period of the previous year.

Net finance expenses also declined by 63.8% to Rs. 188.2 million, compared with Rs. 520 million in the corresponding quarter, reflecting the benefits of the company’s strengthened financial position and reduced financing burden.

Ship repairing emerged as the principal contributor to the improved performance. Revenue from the segment increased by 48.4% to Rs. 3.95 billion, from Rs. 2.66 billion in the corresponding quarter. The segment result at gross profit level more than doubled to Rs. 1.46 billion, compared with Rs. 727 million previously.

While the shipbuilding segment continued to face challenging market and project conditions, its loss at gross profit level narrowed considerably to Rs. 378.8 million, from Rs. 899.6 million in the corresponding period. This improvement helped reduce the impact of the decline in shipbuilding revenue during the quarter.

Managing Director/CEO Thimira S. Godakumbura said: “Returning to quarterly profitability as we mark 52 years of operations represents an important milestone for Colombo Dockyard. The result reflects the commitment of our employees, the strengthening of our ship repair operations, disciplined cost management and the reduction of our financing burden. It also demonstrates the early progress being made through our strategic collaboration with Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited.”

“While we recognise that further work remains, particularly in strengthening our shipbuilding portfolio and improving working capital efficiency, this performance provides greater confidence in the direction of the company. Our focus will remain on building a more resilient, competitive and financially sustainable Colombo Dockyard.”

The company also strengthened its balance sheet during the period. Total Group equity stood at Rs. 15.59 billion as at 30 June 2026, compared with Rs. 4.07 billion a year ago, while stated capital increased to Rs. 13.65 billion. Total assets amounted to Rs. 42.58 billion, with cash and cash equivalents reaching Rs. 8.48 billion.

Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Ltd., presently holds a 51% shareholding in Colombo Dockyard. The company has also aligned its financial year with its parent company, with the current reporting year commencing on 1 April 2026. Accordingly, the results for the three months ended 30 June represent the first quarter under the revised reporting cycle.

“As Colombo Dockyard marks 52 years, the company will continue to prioritise operational excellence, stronger project execution, financial discipline and greater collaboration with Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited. These priorities are expected to support Colombo Dockyard’s long-term competitiveness and reinforce its contribution to Sri Lanka’s maritime and heavy engineering sectors,” the company said.

title: Dayasiri petitions CIABOC to probe Cabinet over judges’ retirement age plan | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 1 August 2026 01:12
-     - 10

Opposition MP Dayasiri Jayasekara

Opposition MP alleges Cabinet decision amounts to bribery and corruption under Anti-Corruption Act

Opposition MP and Attorney-at-Law Dayasiri Jayasekara has petitioned the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) to investigate the Cabinet of Ministers over its decision to extend the retirement age of judges, alleging the proposed constitutional amendment amounts to bribery and corruption under the Anti-Corruption Act, No. 9 of 2023.

In the petition submitted yesterday, Jayasekara argues that the Cabinet’s decision to amend the Constitution to extend the retirement age of judges constitutes an unlawful “gratification”, “favour” or “benefit” to the judiciary and could compromise judicial independence and the separation of powers. 

The petition asks CIABOC to conduct a preliminary inquiry under Section 42 of the Anti-Corruption Act to determine whether there is a prima facie case of bribery or corruption before launching a full investigation into the Cabinet decision. 

Jayasekara cites Sections 93, 100, 104 and 111 of the Anti-Corruption Act, alleging that the proposed extension of judges’ retirement ages could constitute bribery of judicial officers, bribery involving public officials and corruption by public officials. He contends that Cabinet Ministers, as public officials, participated in a decision that would confer a wrongful or unlawful benefit on judges. 

The petition further argues that the proposal could create a conflict of interest if the legislation is challenged before the Supreme Court, as judges who stand to benefit from the amendment could be required to adjudicate on its constitutionality. 

It also claims the proposal is not justified by the administration of justice, asserting that case backlogs are concentrated in the Magistrates’ Courts and District Courts rather than the Supreme Court or Court of Appeal. 

Jayasekara has requested CIABOC to examine Cabinet papers, official documents and communications relating to the proposal, question Cabinet Ministers and other relevant public officials, and, if the amendment proceeds, investigate judges who accept the extension of the retirement age. 

The petition also seeks investigations into officials of the Ministry of Justice and the Legal Draftsman’s Department who may have been involved in preparing the proposal and requests CIABOC to institute proceedings against Cabinet Ministers alleged to have committed corruption under Section 111 of the Anti-Corruption Act. 

In addition, Jayasekara has asked the Commission to direct the Government to refrain from proceeding with the proposed constitutional amendment until the investigation is concluded and to refer any offences disclosed to the appropriate authorities for prosecution.

title: CHEC Port City pitches INR transactions, lagoon-side SEZ incentives to attract Indian investment | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 1 August 2026 01:08
-     - 9

Dedicated hospitality plots and lagoon-front developments positioned for hotel and F&B projects

 Indian firms can register as offshore companies and transact in Indian rupees within SEZ

CHEC Port City Colombo Deputy Managing Director Thulci Aluwihare

Port City Colombo is stepping up efforts to attract Indian investors by promoting its Special Economic Zone (SEZ), the ability to transact in Indian rupees and dedicated hospitality developments, as Sri Lanka seeks to position the project as a regional business gateway.

In an interview with The Economic Times’ ET HospitalityWorld, CHEC Port City Colombo Deputy Managing Director Thulci Aluwihare said the 2.7 sq. km reclamation project was designed to serve as a multi-services export zone rather than solely a real estate development, with India identified as its primary regional growth market. 

The project comprises 91 hectares of common areas, a two-kilometre beach and a 90-hectare swimmable lagoon, alongside mixed-use developments, a yacht marina and a casino.

Aluwihare said the concept evolved after studies of regional real estate developments and SEZs highlighted Sri Lanka’s proximity to India’s economy.

“What the study revealed was that we are next to the largest growth market story, India. We should create a vibrant business district, not necessarily focusing on financial services, but offering a multi-services export zone,” he said.

He said Port City was intended to provide businesses with a platform to access South Asia, including India, adding that Indian rupees are recognised as legal tender within the project’s SEZ framework.

“For an Indian business, without even having to incorporate a new company in Sri Lanka, you can, with your existing company, seek registration as an offshore company and transact in INR. We are trying to seamlessly integrate into that larger economy,” Aluwihare said.

The developer is also targeting hospitality investors by earmarking four dedicated hospitality plots within the master plan.

Aluwihare said the 90-hectare swimmable lagoon would accommodate food and beverage outlets, restaurants and lifestyle retail developments, while the remainder of the project would comprise residential, mixed-use, office, recreation and hotel developments.

According to Aluwihare, the project was initially conceived as a waterfront real estate development before being repositioned as a business district and multi-services export zone aimed at supporting internationally traded services and attracting regional investment.

title: CCPI breaches CBSL  upper-limit, rises to  three-year high 7.3% in July | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 1 August 2026 01:05
-     - 9

Headline inflation measured by the Colombo Consumer Price Index (CCPI accelerated to 7.3% in July, breaching the upper limit of the Central Bank’s 5% ±2 percentage point inflation target range, as non-food price pressures outweighed a moderation in food inflation. 

The Department of Census and Statistics (DCS) yesterday said the year-on-year Colombo Consumer Price Index (CCPI) inflation rate increased to 7.3% in July from 6.8% in June, while the index rose to 208.2 from 207.7. 

This is also a three year high after inflation eased from 12% in June 2023 to 6.3% in July 2023.

Food inflation eased to 6.3% in July from 6.8% in the previous month. However, non-food inflation accelerated to 7.8% from 7.4%, contributing to the increase in headline inflation. 

On a monthly basis, the CCPI increased by 0.2%, with food prices contributing 0.01 percentage points and non-food prices 0.23 percentage points to the increase. 

Core inflation, which excludes the volatile food, energy and transport categories, stood at 4.4% year-on-year in July, while core prices increased 0.8% from the previous month. 

Among the major expenditure categories, transport recorded year-on-year inflation of 17.2%, education 7.2%, non-food items 7.8% and housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels 5.4%. Recreation and culture remained in deflation at negative 2.1%. 

Last month, Central Bank Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe said the Monetary Board expected inflation to move towards the upper end of its 5% target range following administered price adjustments, particularly fuel prices, and responded by raising policy interest rates by 100 basis points in May. 

He said inflation could increase over the following months as the impact of those one-off price adjustments filtered through the economy, but stressed that the effects were expected to be temporary and that inflation was projected to return to the 5% target once those pressures dissipated. 

Dr. Weerasinghe also said the earlier policy tightening was beginning to moderate domestic demand, import growth and credit expansion, which would help contain underlying inflationary pressures.

title: Youth selected for Israeli construction jobs under G2G program to protest next week | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 1 August 2026 01:01
-     - 11

Peaceful demonstration to urge Govt. to address prolonged delays, lack of transparency, and concerns regarding unfair treatment

Nearly 3,000 Sri Lankan youth who have been selected for employment in Israel’s construction sector under the Government-to-Government (G2G) recruitment program are planning a peaceful protest on 6 August 2026, from 9 a.m. to 12:30 p.m., at the Parliament Roundabout, Battaramulla.

The purpose of this protest is to seek the intervention of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to address the prolonged delays, lack of transparency, and concerns regarding unfair treatment in the implementation of the Israel G2G recruitment program.

A statement from the Israel G2G Selected Candidates said that all candidates successfully completed the required professional examinations, interviews, and selection procedures under the G2G program and were officially selected through a transparent lottery conducted by the Israeli authorities. Despite fulfilling every requirement, many have been waiting for more than a year without receiving their employment agreements or any clear explanation regarding the delays.

The protesters are deeply concerned that while thousands of qualified G2G candidates continue to wait, private recruitment agencies appear to be receiving a significantly higher number of job agreements for similar employment opportunities. This situation has raised serious concerns regarding transparency, fairness, and equal treatment by the Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment (SLBFE). Many candidates have invested considerable time, money, and effort in this process, and their families continue to face financial and emotional hardship due to the prolonged uncertainty.

“Our objective is not confrontation but to respectfully appeal to the President to intervene, ensure a transparent review of the recruitment process, address any unfairness, and facilitate a fair and timely solution for all eligible G2G candidates,” the statement added.

title: Harischandra Mills reports impressive 1Q performance with PAT growth of 147% | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 1 August 2026 01:00
-     - 10

Exceptional earnings performance driven by operational efficiencies, volume growth and cost optimisation

 Reinforces sustained value creation through disciplined execution and improved product offerings

Harischandra Mills PLC, an Ambeon Group company, has reported a strong financial performance for 1QFY27, with Profit After Tax (PAT) growing by 147% year-on-year to Rs. 91.8 million.

Revenue increased by 31% to Rs. 1.9 billion, while gross margins expanded to 18% during the quarter. The strong earnings momentum reflects not only the Company’s ability to navigate a challenging macroeconomic environment but also its success in unlocking value across key business segments. 

In a statement, the Company said the robust performance was primarily driven by easing raw material costs, volume growth, operational efficiencies and process improvements. The Food segment, Harischandra’s core operating segment, remained the key driver of topline growth, recording a 22% increase in revenue, supported by both price and volume growth. It also contributed significantly to profitability, with segment operating profit rising by 132% to Rs. 83.2 million, supported by process improvements and enhanced operational efficiencies. Additionally, the company benefited from a decline in agricultural input prices during the quarter.

Chairman Tissa Bandaranayake said: These results were achieved amidst challenging macroeconomic conditions, including inflationary pressures and rising fuel costs linked to global developments. This performance reflects the resilience of our business and the strength of our operating model.”

Executive Director Dr. Sajeeva Narangoda said: “We have a clear roadmap for Harischandra, with a strong focus on process improvements, strengthening our sales channels, and to improve the value propositions across the diverse product range. These initiatives are expected to drive sustained growth in the coming quarters.”

The Board of Directors of Harischandra Mills PLC comprises T. K. Bandaranayake (Chairman), S. N. Samarasinghe (Managing Director), Dr. K. S. Narangoda (Executive Director), L. L. S. Wickremasinghe, S. A. S. Jayasundara, D. T. S. H. Mudalige, P. A. De Silva and S. L. Sebastian.

title: FCCISL congratulates EDB on Sri Lanka’s exports surpassing $ 9 b in first half of 2026 | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 1 August 2026 01:44
-     - 8

FCCISL President  Dr. Rohitha Silva

The Federation of Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Sri Lanka (FCCISL), under the leadership of its President, Dr. Rohitha Silva, together with the Board of Directors and FCCISL State Affairs Committee Chairman Ruwan De Silva in a statement extended its warmest congratulations to Sri Lanka Export Development Board Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Mangala Wijesinghe, and the entire EDB team on the significant achievement of Sri Lanka’s total exports surpassing $ 9 billion during the first half of 2026.

This important national milestone reflects the dedication, commitment and visionary leadership of Mangala Wijesinghe, together with the professionalism and sustained efforts of the EDB team and the resilience, innovation and determination of Sri Lanka’s export community.

 Wijesinghe’s leadership in facilitating export growth, encouraging innovation, addressing longstanding institutional challenges and guiding the sector through increasingly complex and evolving global market conditions is highly commendable. His commitment to strengthening Sri Lanka’s export competitiveness and creating new opportunities for local enterprises represents an important contribution to the country’s economic recovery and future development.

FCCISL also acknowledges with appreciation the active guidance, close cooperation and dedicated leadership extended by Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Minister Sunil Handunnetti, and Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Deputy Minister Chathuranga Abeysinghe. The Federation further recognises the valuable support, commitment and coordination provided by the Secretary to the Ministry and the entire ministry team in creating an enabling institutional and policy environment to advance Sri Lanka’s export sector and broader national economic objectives.

FCCISL firmly believes that increasing export revenue and foreign-exchange earnings is essential to restoring economic stability and placing Sri Lanka on a stronger and more sustainable path towards economic recovery and growth. This is particularly important as the country continues to navigate the cumulative consequences of the Easter Sunday attacks, the COVID-19 pandemic, the prolonged economic crisis and ongoing global conflicts and disruptions affecting international trade, supply chains, energy costs, logistics and access to international markets.

The achievement of an estimated $ 9,012.24 million in combined merchandise and services exports between January and June 2026, representing an 8% year-on-year increase, provides renewed confidence in the resilience, competitiveness and future potential of Sri Lanka’s export sector.

Despite high energy and utility costs, significant tax burdens, and complex statutory and regulatory compliance challenges, this achievement clearly demonstrates the resilience of Sri Lanka’s exporters and the considerable potential of the export sector to expand further and contribute more strongly to national economic recovery and sustainable growth.

The newly formed FCCISL State Affairs Committee, chaired by Ruwan De Silva and functioning under the guidance and leadership of FCCISL President Dr. Rohitha Silva and the Board of Directors, provides an ideal institutional platform for building closer collaboration, constructive engagement and effective cooperation between FCCISL and the Government.

Through FCCISL’s extensive nationwide network of district chambers, sectoral chambers, trade associations, business associations and affiliated institutions, the State Affairs Committee seeks to facilitate structured engagement with the Export Development Board, the Ministry and other relevant public institutions.

This collaborative platform can contribute towards identifying regional and sector-specific business priorities, strengthening exporter readiness, expanding participation in international markets, supporting effective policy coordination and addressing the institutional and operational constraints faced by enterprises throughout the country.

FCCISL said it looks forward to engaging more actively and constructively with the Export Development Board under the visionary leadership of Mangala Wijesinghe. The Federation wishes to work closely with the EDB, the Ministry and other relevant stakeholders to promote innovation, facilitate market expansion, strengthen regional enterprises and enable businesses across Sri Lanka to contribute more effectively to the country’s export and economic-development objectives.

FCCISL said it remains committed to building a strong and meaningful partnership between the public and private sectors and supporting the achievement of Sri Lanka’s future export targets through its nationwide district and sectoral chamber network.

title: Registrations open for  Sri Lanka Economic and Investment Summit 2026 | Daily FT
summary:

-     - 7

Held on 12 and 13 Oct., this year’s theme is: Positioning Sri Lanka in a Changing Global Economy: Resilience, Reform, and the Future of Economic Policy

The Ceylon Chamber of Commerce has announced that registrations are now open for the Sri Lanka Economic and Investment Summit 2026 (SLEIS 2026), taking place on 12 and 13 October at the Shangri-La Colombo.

Held under the theme “Positioning Sri Lanka in a Changing Global Economy: Resilience, Reform, and the Future of Economic Policy,” this year’s summit comes at a defining point in Sri Lanka’s economic journey as the country looks beyond stabilisation towards sustained, private sector-led growth and greater integration with regional and global markets.

Recognised as one of the country’s premier economic forums, the two-day summit will bring together senior government leaders, policymakers, business leaders, investors, development partners, and international experts, for two days of dialogue on Sri Lanka’s economic outlook, reform agenda and investment opportunities. 

Through high-level discussions and strategic engagement, the summit will explore how Sri Lanka can strengthen competitiveness, attract investment, expand exports and position itself within Asia’s evolving growth networks.

SLEIS 2026 will feature keynote addresses, high-level panel discussions, sector-focused conversations, investor engagement opportunities and business networking designed to facilitate constructive dialogue between the public and private sectors. 

The program will examine the policies, partnerships and investment opportunities that can accelerate Sri Lanka’s next phase of economic growth, with further details on the agenda, speakers and sessions to be announced in the coming weeks.

The Ceylon Chamber encourages early registration, as the Summit has consistently attracted strong participation from local and international delegates, and reaches full capacity well in advance. Register at https://sleis.chamber.lk/.

summary:

Opposition Leader 

Sajith Premadasa

The forum will focus on challenges facing the species, including habitat fragmentation, snaring, poisoning, road fatalities and other forms of wildlife crime, while promoting greater collaboration on conservation policy, scientific research and public awareness.

title: Lieutenant General Nilantha Premaratne appointed 26th Army Commander | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 1 August 2026 01:37
-     - 10

Army Major General 

Nilantha Premaratne

President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has appointed Chief of Staff of the Sri Lanka Army Major General Nilantha Premaratne as the 26th Commander of the Sri Lanka Army, with the promotion to Lieutenant General with effect from today.

The letter of appointment was presented to Lieutenant General Premaratne by Secretary to the President Dr. Nandika Sanath Kumanayake at the Presidential Secretariat yesterday.

The appointment follows the retirement of incumbent Army Commander General Lasantha Rodrigo. Lieutenant General Premaratne joined the Sri Lanka Army as an Officer Cadet in 1990 and was commissioned as a Second Lieutenant in 1992 after completing basic military training at the Sri Lanka Military Academy, Diyatalawa.

He was subsequently posted to the Sri Lanka Artillery Regiment and has completed a 36-year military career, during which he held senior command and staff positions.

Lieutenant General Premaratne holds a Master’s degree in Defence Studies from the Naval Postgraduate School in California, United States, and a Master of Defence Studies degree from the University of Kelaniya.

He has also completed professional and specialist military training programs in Sri Lanka and overseas.

In recognition of his service during the humanitarian operation, Lieutenant General Premaratne has been awarded the Rana Sura Padakkama (RSP) on two occasions. He has also received the Uttama Seva Padakkama (USP) for distinguished service to the Sri Lanka Army.
